GB.language: English (Welsh is also official in Wales)
GB.tipping: Around 10–12.5% in sit-down restaurants if service isn’t already on the bill; tipping in pubs is optional.
GB.safety: Generally safe; watch for pickpockets in busy centres and on public transport, and plan a licensed taxi or night bus home.
GB.cards: Contactless cards and phones are accepted almost everywhere, including most buses and city rail.

IE.tipping: 10–15% for good table service is common; not expected for drinks at the bar.
IE.safety: Generally safe; keep valuables close in busy nightlife streets and use licensed taxis.

PT.tipping: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving 5–10% for good table service is appreciated.
PT.safety: Low crime overall; pickpocketing happens on busy trams and at viewpoints. Respect red flags and lifeguard advice on beaches.
PT.cards: Cards are widely accepted; keep a little cash for small cafés and markets. Bread, olives and starters put on the table (couvert) are charged if eaten.

ES.language: Spanish (plus Catalan, Basque, Galician or Valencian regionally)
ES.tipping: Not expected; rounding up or leaving 5–10% for good service is a kind extra.
ES.safety: Generally safe; pickpocketing is the main risk on busy streets, beaches and metro lines. Dinner starts late, often after 21:00.
ES.cards: Cards and contactless are widely accepted.

FR.tipping: Service is included by law (service compris); leaving small change or up to 5–10% for great service is optional.
FR.safety: Generally safe; be alert to pickpockets on metros, at major sights and around big stations.
FR.cards: Cards are widely accepted; some small bakeries prefer cash for small amounts.

NL.tipping: Optional; rounding up or 5–10% for good table service.
NL.safety: Generally safe; watch for cyclists in bike lanes and pickpockets in crowded centres.
NL.cards: Debit cards and contactless are standard; some places do not accept cash or credit cards, so carry a debit card.

DE.tipping: Round up or add 5–10% when you pay, telling the server the total rather than leaving money on the table.
DE.safety: Generally safe; keep an eye on bags at big stations and festivals.
DE.cards: Card acceptance has improved but some bars, bakeries and small restaurants are still cash-only.

IT.tipping: Not expected; a cover charge (coperto) or service may appear on the bill. Leaving a few euros for great service is fine.
IT.safety: Generally safe; pickpockets work busy sights, trams and stations. Validate regional train tickets before boarding where required.
IT.cards: Cards are widely accepted; carry some cash for small cafés and markets.

CZ.tipping: Around 10% for good table service is customary.
CZ.safety: Generally safe; use official exchange offices with clear rates, avoid street money changers and check the bill.
CZ.cards: Cards are widely accepted; when paying by card abroad, choose to be charged in the local currency.

AT.tipping: Round up or add around 5–10% when paying.
AT.safety: Very safe overall; usual care with bags in busy areas.
AT.cards: Cards are widely accepted, though some traditional cafés and bars prefer cash.

HU.tipping: 10–15% is customary unless a service charge is already on the bill.
HU.safety: Generally safe; check menus show prices, use official taxis and avoid street money changers.
HU.cards: Cards are widely accepted; choose to pay in forints when asked.

BE.tipping: Service is usually included; rounding up for good service is appreciated.
BE.safety: Generally safe; watch for pickpockets around big stations and busy squares.
BE.cards: Cards and contactless are widely accepted.

CH.language: German, French, Italian and Romansh (by region)
CH.tipping: Service is included; rounding up is a polite extra.
CH.safety: Very safe; prices are high, so check costs before ordering.
CH.cards: Cards are widely accepted; euros are not always accepted, and change is given in francs.

DK.tipping: Service is included; rounding up for good service is optional.
DK.safety: Very safe; give way to the many cyclists.
DK.cards: Very card-friendly; many places prefer cards to cash.

SE.tipping: Service is included; rounding up or around 5–10% for good service is optional.
SE.safety: Very safe; usual city care at night.
SE.cards: Largely cashless: many cafés, buses and venues accept cards only.

NO.tipping: Service is included; rounding up for good service is optional.
NO.safety: Very safe; dress for changeable weather.
NO.cards: Largely cashless; cards are accepted almost everywhere.

FI.tipping: Not expected; rounding up is optional.
FI.safety: Very safe; winter days are short and icy, so wear good footwear.

EE.tipping: Around 5–10% for good table service is appreciated but not required.
EE.safety: Generally safe; check bills in old-town bars aimed at tourists.

LV.safety: Generally safe; check drink prices before ordering in old-town bars.

LT.safety: Generally safe; usual care at night.

PL.tipping: Around 10% for good table service; saying “thank you” when handing over cash can mean “keep the change”.
PL.safety: Generally safe; check drink prices and avoid touts offering clubs or bars.
PL.cards: Cards are widely accepted; pay in złoty when asked.

SI.tipping: Rounding up or around 10% for good service.

HR.tipping: Around 10% for good table service is appreciated.
HR.safety: Generally safe; drink water and use sun protection in summer heat.
HR.cards: Cards are widely accepted; carry some cash for small kiosks and islands.

RO.safety: Generally safe; use ride-hailing apps or official taxis with clear meters.
RO.cards: Cards are widely accepted in cities.

BG.safety: Generally safe; use reputable taxi firms with clear meters.
BG.cards: Cards are widely accepted in cities; carry a little cash elsewhere.

GR.tipping: Not obligatory; rounding up or 5–10% for good service is appreciated.
GR.safety: Generally safe; drink water and avoid the midday sun in summer, and watch for pickpockets on busy metros.
GR.cards: Cards are widely accepted; carry cash for small kiosks and island tavernas.

MT.safety: Very safe; traffic drives on the left.

CY.language: Greek (Turkish in the north; English widely spoken)
CY.tipping: Around 10% if service isn’t already included.
CY.safety: Generally safe; traffic drives on the left. Respect the UN buffer zone and crossing-point rules if you visit the north.
